note: FHE noise-budget mechanism parameters and measured PPML latencies. Scheme figures (bootstrap cost, gate/level model) and per-model FHE-vs-MPC latencies are drawn from the article's cited primary sources. The sawtooth mechanism is a first-order model of leveled evaluation + bootstrapping; the per-model latency/memory figures are measured values, not model output.

schemes.label: CKKS
schemes.bootstrapNote: functional bootstrap ≈ 1 min (9-bit LUT), ≈ 10 min (12-bit LUT)
schemes.strength: linear layers (matmul) are fast — one ciphertext packs thousands of slots
schemes.weakness: nonlinear (ReLU/softmax) needs polynomial approx or a switch to TFHE

schemes.label: TFHE
schemes.bootstrapNote: ≈ 1 ms per Boolean gate (sub-ms on GPU); noise stays bounded unconditionally
schemes.weakness: no SIMD: one 768×768 matmul is ~590k separately-bootstrapped gates

models.label: LogReg
models.note: shallow — evaluates entirely inside the initial noise budget, no bootstrap

models.label: BERT-Tiny
models.note: 2 transformer layers fit leveled CKKS; at the optimistic end nearly tied with MPC

models.label: ResNet-20
models.note: 20-layer CNN evaluates in leveled CKKS without bootstrapping

models.label: BERT-Base
models.note: 12 transformer layers exceed any practical noise budget — bootstrapping unavoidable
